summary: A solid progressive delivery control plane centered on a transactional state machine in Postgres with leases, optimistic concurrency, idempotent reconciliation, and metrics-based step analysis. It cleanly supports canary/blue-green/rolling, multi-target sequencing, durable auditability, and at-least-once event delivery with an outbox pattern. Overall it’s plausibly production-ready, with some missing depth around security and hard scaling/HA edges.
strengths: Strong correctness story (CAS lock_version, DB leases, idempotency keys) that prevents double-promotes and makes retries safe
Good operational/rollout safety design (burn-rate guardrails, inconclusive handling, policy snapshots, outbox events, break-glass rollback paths)
weaknesses: Security and multi-tenancy details are underspecified (authn/z, RBAC model, secret management, webhook key rotation, audit tamper-resistance, supply-chain attestations)

Scalability/HA edge cases need more concreteness (DB contention/indexing, horizontal scaling of the worker loop and timers, Kubernetes/metrics rate limiting at fleet scale, and the practicality of RPO 0 across regions)
